name: Valley Woodworkers
old_description: The Valley Woodworkers of West Virginia cares about our community and does what we can to improve it.  The mission of the Valley Woodworkers of West Virginia is twofold.  One part is the training of local community members to be woodworker. Whether it be honing their craft to later become a professional woodworker, or merely to create handcrafted heirloom pieces for their friends and family.  Secondly, since 1991, the Valley Woodworkers have been making heirloom quality wooden toys for the Salvation Army to distribute to underprivileged children at Christmas.
about:
Valley Woodworkers operates from Dunbar, West Virginia. The organization was founded in 2008 and functions as a woodworking club open to all skill levels. Its origins trace to a dual mission: training local residents in woodworking crafts and producing heirloom-quality wooden toys for the Salvation Army’s Christmas distribution to underprivileged children, a program ongoing since 1991.

The club holds monthly meetings on the second Thursday at its clubhouse on 12th Street, featuring project show-and-tell sessions and technical demonstrations. Beyond member education, volunteers manufacture wooden toys year-round for charitable donation. The facility serves as a gathering point rather than a commercial production shop; no headcount, square footage, or output volumes are published.

Participants range from beginners to professional woodworkers, while the toy program benefits children served by the Salvation Army. Local businesses such as Woodcraft and Withrow Supply in Huntington provide sponsorship and material support, including finishes, machinery, hardware, and sharpening services.

The group emphasizes community improvement through skill-sharing and charitable giving. Its distinguishing feature is the long-standing commitment to producing handcrafted toys for children in need, coupled with an open-door policy that welcomes anyone with an interest in woodworking.
